# An interval split at its midpoint, one-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_split_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Two intervals that together are $X = [x_l, x_u]$, split at a point of it:

$$X = [a_l, a_u] \cup [b_l, b_u].$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.split()` | `Interval<T, 1>` | `Split<Interval<T, 1>>` | `left` is $[a_l, a_u]$ and `right` is $[b_l, b_u]$; they meet at a point of $X$, which is not claimed to be the midpoint; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $[x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $[a_l, a_u]$ and $[b_l, b_u]$ are canonical intervals.
- If $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is empty, both are.
- Otherwise neither is, $a_l = x_l$, $b_u = x_u$ and $a_u = b_l$: the two together are $X$, split at that point, which is in $X$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_split_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_split_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_split_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the bounds and the midpoint of interval_mid_rad_1 (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_split_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_split_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`interval_mid_rad_1`](interval_mid_rad_1.md).

```
# An interval with one-limb bounds split at its midpoint (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", the row of split() and "The empty set and the whole line"): [xl, m] and [m, xu], m the
# midpoint of interval_mid_rad_1, which is in [xl, xu]; their union is the interval. The whole line
# gives [-inf, 0] and [0, +inf], a half-line [l, +inf] gives [l, Omega] and [Omega, +inf], and the
# empty set the empty set twice, told by its radius, a NaN.

(m, r) = interval_mid_rad_1(xl, xu)
ne     = eq(r, r)
mi     = neg(const inf)
al     = copy(xl)
au     = select(ne, m, mi)
bl     = select(ne, m, const inf)
bu     = copy(xu)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#interval_split_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 4 domains of 4 formats | 581 154 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
